sourceType: Image-generated front-gait corrections, technically packed into existing generated directional atlases.

prompts.rowanFrontFootfallPrompt: Edit this FRONT-FACING walk sprite strip into a physically correct alternating-leg cycle. Keep exact SAME character identity, painted style, head/body ratio, costume, colours, lighting and props. Exactly EIGHT FULL-BODY frames in ONE horizontal row on transparent background. Every character's head and torso face DIRECTLY TOWARDS VIEWER, never sideways. Same apparent stature and cell baseline, no resizing character betweenframes. The8poses MUST alternate two different legs. Anatomical names confuse this; obey SCREEN COORDINATES: FRAME1 foremost sole is the boot on SCREEN LEFT, the boot on SCREEN RIGHT stays behind. FRAME2 screenleft boot planted, screenright heel lifting. FRAME3 SCREEN RIGHT KNEE lifted in front, screenleftleg straight supporting. FRAME4 screenrightboot swinging towardsviewer. FRAME5 foremost sole is boot on SCREEN RIGHT (OPPOSITE OF FRAME1), screenleftboot behind. FRAME6 screenrightboot planted, screenleftheel lifting. FRAME7 SCREEN LEFT KNEE lifted in front, screenrightleg straight supporting (OPPOSITE OF FRAME3). FRAME8 screenleftboot swings towardsviewer. Make legs visibly separated, both boots visible and moving, no duplicate lead foot atframes1and5! Subtle weight shift and arm/garment counter-swing. Keep props in same hands so NO image mirroring to fake feet. Full eightphase loop from1through8backto1. 8evenlyspaced equalcells, generous transparent margins atall sides, no clipping. No text, labels, arrows, gridlines, ground shadows or background. Rowan is the friendly straw scarecrow carpenter with green broad-brim hat, burgundy scarf, patchworkcoat, brown work apron and wooden mallet. His trousers end below knees; show boots well. Do not alter his round button-eye face.

prompts.rowanFixPrompt: Edit this 8sprite strip, preserving first5frames EXACTLY. Correct the LAST THREE figures (6th,7th,8th) into opposite-leg phases. All figures MUST HAVE EXACTLY TWO LEGS AND TWO BOOTS. Sixthfigure: SCREEN RIGHT boot planted straight underbody with weight, SCREEN LEFT heel lifts fromground behind. Seventhfigure: SCREEN LEFT knee is raised forwards with SCREEN LEFT BOOT offground, SCREEN RIGHT leg stays straight and its boot planted; remove the extra third foot currently visible! Eighthfigure: SCREEN LEFT boot swings forward towardsviewer ready forcontact, SCREEN RIGHT staysback. Do not change torso/head/clothing/hat/mallet/face orframeheight. Keep correct first5figures unchanged, exactpaintedstyle andproportions, eight equal spaced fullbodycells. Genuine alternating gait. Transparent background only, nofloor orshadows; existing transparency preserved. Only8figuresinonerow.

prompts.vesperPhaseFixPrompt: Fix just the FOURTH and SIXTH figures in this eight-frame vampire walk cycle. Other six figures unchanged. Fourth figure: SCREEN RIGHT boot is swinging FORWARD towards viewer, SCREEN LEFT boot remains planted behind. The extended boot MUST be on the RIGHT side of this figure, not the left. Sixth figure: SCREEN RIGHT leg is straight supporting his weight with right boot on ground, SCREEN LEFT heel lifts behind readyto raise leftknee in nextfigure. Preserve all SAME head and torso proportions, costume, face, candelabrum, hand placement, exact style and size. Eight figures in one horizontal row. No mirror because props and face must remain in original hands. Everyfigure exactly2legs2boots. Keep transparency, no background/no groundshadow/no labels. Renderonlythe8figurestripwithsamecellspacing andbodyheight.

notes: The first Rowan front correction contained an extra boot in passing pose6; that frame is excluded and replaced with the existing authored left-pass pose from original Rowan atlas row0,col3.
Vesper background removal and phase3/5 corrections were performed with image generation.

Elowen original directional source is retained as elowen-before-front-repair.png. New front sprites preserve overall stature but frontal painting details vary slightly across independently generated viewpoints.
